row.notes: F1SuspensionDamage impact callback, registered by 0x144653ad0 (lea at 0x144653bb9). param_1 = the F1SuspensionDamage system (CarLive+0x5d0). Ignores impacts below max(SpeedThreshold +0x28^+0x30, ...); scales front-corner impacts by FrontDamageScale (+0x38^+0x40) and rear-corner impacts by RearDamageScale (+0x48^+0x50); sets flag 4 (collider tag CAR_, 0x5f524143) or 8 (any other collider) at +0x20 of the matched SuspensionSystem wheel ([CarLive+0x580]+0x70..+0x88 matched by +0x2b4/+0x2b8), not at system +0x20, with the impact speed at wheel+0x24/+0x2c, gated by CarLive+0x133 bit 1 and +0x130 bit 3 (corrected per V1318). Every value is read on each hit, so a live write applies to the next impact. Cross-checked 2026-10-28 against the private findings of Will (william09leo, Heavier Damage), which agree. See car.md#damage. | 2026-11-13 susp-collision (static, Steam): (susp_damage, contact) from the code: rcx is the system (its +8 is the CarLive), rdx the contact record, and r8/r9 are written before any read. The only ref is lea rsi at 0x144653bb6 in the system's Init 0x144653ad0, which (only when its reset argument dl is 0) hands {fn, this} to the listener remove thunk 0x1446510d0 (body 0x155338ff0) and then Car_Collision_AddListener 0x144651f90 (body 0x155339950) (15 slots of {fn, ctx} at CarLive+0x9db8). Car_Collision_Dispatch calls each slot as fn(ctx, &contact) at 0x14473fd28 under the car's lock [car+0xf0] and ignores the return, so the return is void. Contact: +0 CarLive, +8 the car's own hit body, +0x18 contact point*, +0x20 normal*, +0x30 the other collider (dword tag CAR_ for a car), +0x38 f32 scaled by the front or rear damage scale, +0x40 u8. EA: the same bytes at rva 0x464afa0, only ref lea at 0x144649e46. Wrappable binding for addons (Will, Heavier Damage); V9284 agrees.
